tort_pain_suffering.summary: UK Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (2024) value tetraplegia/quadriplegia (complete paralysis of all four limbs) PSLA at GBP396,140-GBP493,000 (~USD503,000-USD626,000 at 1.27), the top non-fatal suffering bracket in English tort; midpoint ~USD565,000 prices the suffering of permanent total paralysis.

tort_pain_suffering.summary: UK Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (2024) value very severe brain damage (little/no meaningful response to environment, double incontinence, need for full-time nursing care) PSLA at GBP344,150-GBP493,000 (~USD437,000-USD626,000); midpoint ~USD531,000 prices the suffering of catastrophic permanent brain injury just short of death.
tort_pain_suffering.source_citation: Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (Apr 2024), Ch.3(A)(a); 16th-ed GBP219,070-GBP403,990 uplifted to 17th-ed GBP344,150-GBP493,000 confirmed by Morton Fraser MacRoberts 2024 JCG summary https://www.mfmac.com/insights/personal-injury/judicial-college-guidelines-in-personal-injury-claims-2024/

tort_pain_suffering.summary: UK Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (2024) value moderately severe brain injury (very serious disability, substantial dependence on care, marked intellectual/personality impairment) PSLA at GBP267,340-GBP344,150 (~USD339,500-USD437,000); midpoint ~USD388,000.
tort_pain_suffering.source_citation: Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (Apr 2024), Ch.3(A)(b); bracket GBP267,340-GBP344,150 reported by Mooneerams Solicitors https://www.mooneerams.com/blog/guide-to-traumatic-brain-injury-compensation-claims/ . tort_pain_suffering.summary: UK Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (2024) value total blindness (loss of sight in both eyes) PSLA in the region of GBP327,940 (~USD416,000), pricing the permanent loss of all sight as suffering; sits just below the GBP493,000 'total blindness and deafness' category.
tort_pain_suffering.source_citation: Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (2024) value loss of sight in one eye WITH some reduced vision in the remaining eye at GBP117,150-GBP219,400 (~USD148,800-USD278,600); midpoint ~USD214,000. tort_pain_suffering.source_citation: Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. tort_pain_suffering.summary: UK Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (2024) value moderate PTSD (largely recovered, any continuing effects not grossly disabling) at GBP9,980-GBP28,250 (~USD12,700-USD35,900); midpoint ~USD24,000.
tort_pain_suffering.source_citation: Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (Apr 2024), Ch.4(B); bracket GBP9,980-GBP28,250 confirmed via WebSearch of JCG 17th-ed PTSD brackets and compensationcalculatoruk.co.uk https://www.compensationcalculatoruk.co.uk/list-of-compensation-payouts-in-the-uk/

tort_pain_suffering.summary: UK Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (2024) value less severe PTSD (virtually full recovery within 1-2 years, only minor symptoms persisting) at GBP4,820-GBP9,980 (~USD6,100-USD12,700); midpoint ~USD9,400 - the floor of the PTSD suffering<->money ladder.
tort_pain_suffering.source_citation: Judicial College Guidelines 17th ed. (Apr 2024), Ch.4(B); bracket GBP4,820-GBP9,980 confirmed via WebSearch of JCG 17th-ed PTSD brackets and compensationcalculatoruk.co.uk https://www.compensationcalculatoruk.co.uk/list-of-compensation-payouts-in-the-uk/

tort_pain_suffering.summary: The UK Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012 fixed tariff sets the maximum single-injury payment at GBP250,000 (Level A20, ~USD317,500 at 1.27) - the statutory cap, awarded for the worst survivable injuries: quadriplegia/tetraplegia substantially complete to both upper and lower limb levels, and the most severe brain injury; a fixed, no-fault price far below court PSLA awards for the same injuries (~GBP493k JCG), showing strong concavity/cap behaviour in a statutory scheme.
tort_pain_suffering.source_citation: Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012, Annex E Part A; gov.uk official guidance confirms A20 = GBP250,000 = 'quadriplegia/tetraplegia substantially complete to both upper and lower limb levels' and most-severe brain injury https://www.gov.uk/guidance/criminal-injuries-compensation-scheme-injury-payments . NOTE: 'very serious brain injury' is the lower A19 (GBP175,000); only the most severe brain-injury category reaches A20.

tort_pain_suffering.summary: The UK Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012 fixed tariff pays GBP175,000 (Level A19, ~USD222,250) for substantially complete paraplegia (impairment of motor/sensory function of the lower extremities), one statutory step below the A20 cap.
tort_pain_suffering.source_citation: Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012, Annex E Part A; gov.uk official guidance confirms paraplegia 'substantially complete' = A19 = GBP175,000 https://www.gov.uk/guidance/criminal-injuries-compensation-scheme-injury-payments

tort_pain_suffering.summary: The UK Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012 fixed tariff pays GBP110,000 (Level A18, ~USD139,700) for moderately severe brain damage (serious disablement of physical/mental faculties requiring substantial dependence on care, marked impairment of intellect and personality).
tort_pain_suffering.source_citation: Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012, Annex E Part A; gov.uk official guidance confirms moderately severe brain damage = A18 = GBP110,000 https://www.gov.uk/guidance/criminal-injuries-compensation-scheme-injury-payments

tort_pain_suffering.summary: The UK Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012 fixed tariff pays GBP110,000 (Level A18, ~USD139,700) for total loss of sight in both eyes (blindness), equating permanent total blindness to moderately severe brain damage in this statutory ladder.
tort_pain_suffering.label_raw: Loss of sight - both eyes (Level A18)
tort_pain_suffering.source_citation: Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012, Annex E Part A; gov.uk official guidance confirms loss of sight in both eyes = A18 = GBP110,000 https://www.gov.uk/guidance/criminal-injuries-compensation-scheme-injury-payments

tort_pain_suffering.summary: The UK Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012 fixed tariff pays GBP22,000 (Level A12, ~USD27,940) for total loss of sight in one eye - one fifth of the GBP110,000 paid for both eyes, a clean within-scheme single-vs-double concavity point.
tort_pain_suffering.label_raw: Loss of sight - one eye (Level A12)
tort_pain_suffering.source_citation: Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012, Annex E Part A; gov.uk official guidance confirms loss of sight in one eye = A12 = GBP22,000 https://www.gov.uk/guidance/criminal-injuries-compensation-scheme-injury-payments

tort_pain_suffering.summary: The UK Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012 fixed tariff pays GBP27,000 (Level A13, ~USD34,290) for permanent, seriously disabling mental injury (confirmed by psychiatrist/clinical psychologist) - the scheme's top pure-psychological tariff, a no-fault floor for severe permanent psychological suffering.
tort_pain_suffering.label_raw: Permanent mental injury, seriously disabling (Level A13)
tort_pain_suffering.source_citation: Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012, Annex E Part A; gov.uk official guidance confirms permanent mental injury 'seriously disabling' = A13 = GBP27,000 (moderately disabling = A11 = GBP19,000) https://www.gov.uk/guidance/criminal-injuries-compensation-scheme-injury-payments

tort_pain_suffering.summary: The UK Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012 fixed tariff floor is GBP1,000 (Level A1, ~USD1,270), the minimum award - covering e.g. disabling mental injury lasting 6 weeks up to 28 weeks, permanent slight loss of visual field, simple/minor fractures - the bottom anchor of the 25-level statutory suffering<->money scale that runs A1=GBP1,000 to A20=GBP250,000.
tort_pain_suffering.source_citation: Criminal Injuries Compensation Scheme 2012, Annex E; gov.uk official guidance confirms A1 = GBP1,000 is the lowest level and that 'disabling mental injury lasting 6 weeks or more up to 28 weeks' is an A1 (GBP1,000) injury https://www.gov.uk/guidance/criminal-injuries-compensation-scheme-injury-payments ; A1-GBP1,000 to A20-GBP250,000 range corroborated by cica-uk.co.uk and multiple secondary tables.

day_fines.summary: German StGB Section 40 sets a fine as 5 to 360 daily units (severity/culpability), each unit valued from EUR 1 to EUR 30,000 (about USD 1 to USD 32,400 in 2024) based on the offender's net income per day; the count encodes severity and the per-unit value encodes the money metric.
day_fines.label_raw: StGB Section 40 daily-unit count (5-360) and unit value (EUR 1-30,000)
day_fines.source_citation: German Criminal Code (StGB) Section 40, lewik.org/term/15370 (verbatim: 'minimum fine shall consist of five and ... maximum ... three hundred and sixty full daily units'; 'A daily unit shall not be set at less than one and not at more than thirty thousand euros') and official translation gesetze-im-internet.de/englisch_stgb.

day_fines.summary: In Germany an unpaid day-fine converts to substitute prison time: historically 1 day-unit = 1 day in prison, and since the 1 Feb 2024 reform 2 day-units = 1 day in prison, giving an explicit legal exchange rate between roughly two days of disposable income and one day of lost liberty.
day_fines.label_raw: Ersatzfreiheitsstrafe conversion: pre-2024 1 unit=1 prison day; post-2024 2 units=1 prison day
day_fines.source_citation: KFN (Kriminologisches Forschungsinstitut Niedersachsen) study on the Section 43 StGB reform, en.kfn.de/research-projects/ersatzfreiheitsstrafe: conversion shifted to '2:1 ... two daily fine rates correspond to one day of imprisonment', effective 1 February 2024; previously 1:1. Corroborated by KriPoZ commentary (kripoz.de, Feb 2024).

day_fines.summary: German day-unit counts form an empirical severity ladder: ~42% of 2018 fine cases were under 30 units and ~49% were 31-90 units, and a fine over 90 daily units is the threshold above which the conviction appears on the certificate of conduct (Fuehrungszeugnis), pricing relative offence seriousness on the 5-360 scale.
day_fines.label_raw: ordinary offences 30-90 units; >90 units = entry on Fuehrungszeugnis (criminal record)
day_fines.source_citation: Mitali Nagrecha, 'The Limits of Fairer Fines: Lessons from Germany' (Criminal Justice Policy Program, Harvard Law School / Fines and Fees Justice Center, 2020), finesandfeesjusticecenter.org: '42% of all cases ... less than 30 units and another 49% ... between 31 and 90 units'. Record threshold: German Federal Office of Justice (bundesjustizamt.de) / criminal-law-germany.lawyer 'When do I have a criminal record in Germany?': fines of '90 daily rates or more' are entered on the Fuehrungszeugnis.

day_fines.summary: A Finnish day-fine equals about half of daily disposable income, where disposable income is ~1/60 of monthly net income after a EUR 255 living allowance, with a EUR 6 floor per unit; a single offence carries 1 to 120 day-units (240 if multiple offences combined) and a speeding fine is at least EUR 115, separating income-scaled money from severity-scaled count.
day_fines.label_raw: day-unit = 1/2 of (monthly net /60) after EUR 255 allowance; range 1-120 units (240 combined); floor EUR 6/unit; speeding min EUR 115
day_fines.source_citation: Wikipedia 'Day-fine' (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Day-fine), verbatim: 'the day-fine is one half of daily disposable income ... one 60th part of the person's monthly mean income ... after ... a basic living allowance of EUR 255'; 'minimum of 1 day-fine, up to a maximum of 120 day-fines ... 240 day-fines' if combined; 'minimum amount of a day-fine is 6 euros'; 'For speeding ... the fine is at least ... EUR 115' (~USD 124 in 2024).

day_fines.summary: Finnish multimillionaire Anders Wiklof was fined EUR 121,000 (about USD 131,000 in 2024) in 2023 for driving 82 km/h in a 50 km/h zone, a single low-severity offence whose few day-units became enormous solely because the per-unit value tracks his very high income (no cap).
day_fines.label_raw: speeding 82 in 50 km/h zone; EUR 121,000 fine + 10-day licence suspension
day_fines.source_citation: ABC News (abcnews.com/ABCNews/finnish-businessman-handed-121000-speeding-ticket, story id 99861907, 2023): fine 'EUR 121,000', '82 kilometers per hour ... 50 km/h' zone (Aland), plus a 10-day driving-licence suspension; report also notes a prior EUR 63,680 fine (2013) and an earlier EUR 95,000 fine. CAUTION: the original collector citation transposed the prior-fine years/amounts ('EUR 63,000 (2018) and EUR 95,000 (2013)') -- per ABC the 2013 fine was EUR 63,680 and the EUR 95,000 fine was several years earlier (~2008); the headline 2023 figure is correct.

day_fines.summary: A Finnish businessman was fined EUR 112,000 (about USD 160,000 in 2024 after FX and inflation) in 2009 for driving 82 km/h in a 60 km/h zone, illustrating how the same trivial-harm offence scales to six figures purely via the income-indexed per-unit value.
day_fines.label_raw: speeding 82 in 60 km/h zone; EUR 112,000 fine
day_fines.source_citation: Wikipedia 'Day-fine' (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Day-fine), verbatim: 'In 2009 a businessman was fined EUR 112,000 for travelling at 82 kilometres per hour in an area with a speed limit of 60 kilometres per hour.' (~USD 160,000 normalized to 2024 via EUR x1.08 + ~30% cumulative inflation 2009-2024; the USD figure is the collector's estimate, not a sourced number).

day_fines.summary: A Finnish (Nokia) businessman with a ~EUR 10 million yearly income received only 6 day-units in 2001 but a total of EUR 26,000 (about USD 43,000 in 2024) for running a red light, showing that with severity (unit count) held very low the total money is set almost entirely by income.
day_fines.source_citation: Wikipedia 'Day-fine' (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Day-fine), verbatim: 'a Finnish businessman with a yearly income of 10 million euros, received a relatively mild punishment of six day-fines, amounting EUR 26,000' for running a red light. (~USD 43,000 normalized to 2024; USD figure is the collector's estimate.)

day_fines.summary: Swedish day-fines run 30 to 150 units (up to 200 for multiple offences) with each unit valued from SEK 50 to SEK 1,000 (about USD 5 to USD 95 in 2024), one unit being roughly one-thousandth of annual income; unlike Finland the per-unit value is capped, bounding the money axis.
day_fines.label_raw: 30-150 units (200 combined); SEK 50-1,000 per unit; ~1/1000 of annual income; total floor SEK 750
day_fines.source_citation: Swedish Penal Code (Brottsbalken) Chapter 25 on fines, as summarized by TheLocal.se (thelocal.se/20240423, 2024) and Swedish legal sources (domarbloggen.se, aklagare.se): number of day-fines 'at least thirty and at most one hundred fifty ... up to two hundred' for joint sentences; each day-fine 'a minimum of 50 kronor and a maximum of 1,000 kronor'; 'one daily fine ... equivalent to one thousandth of the yearly income'. SEK 50/1000 ~ USD 5 / USD 95 (SEK->USD x0.095, 2024). CORRECTED: collector stated SEK 30 floor; current statutory minimum is SEK 50 (the SEK 30 floor is an outdated figure). Collector's Wikipedia 'Day-fine' citation does not contain these Swedish figures and was replaced.

day_fines.summary: Danish Penal Code violations are punishable by up to 60 day-fines, with the fine halved (minimum DKK 500, about USD 73 in 2024) for offenders under 18 or whose gross annual income does not exceed DKK 171,795 (2020), giving a lower severity ceiling than Germany/Finland plus an explicit income-based reduction band.
day_fines.label_raw: up to 60 day-units; halve if gross income <= DKK 171,795/yr or under 18; floor DKK 500
day_fines.source_citation: Wikipedia 'Day-fine' (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Day-fine), verbatim: 'may be punishable by up to 60 day-fines'; reduced 'by half (to a minimum of DKK 500)' for offenders under 18 or 'whose gross annual income does not exceed DKK 171,795 (as of 2020)'. DKK 500 ~ USD 73 (DKK->USD x0.145, 2024).

day_fines.summary: A Swedish motorist in Switzerland in 2010 was fined CHF 3,600 per day for 300 days, more than EUR 1,000,000 total (CHF ~1.08 million; about USD 1.36 million in 2024) for driving ~290 km/h, the extreme high end showing day-unit count (300, near the ceiling) multiplied by an income-indexed per-day value can rival serious-injury compensation in magnitude.
day_fines.label_raw: speeding ~290 km/h; CHF 3,600/day x 300 day-units = CHF ~1.08M (>EUR 1,000,000)
day_fines.source_citation: SWI swissinfo.ch ('Driver faces $1,000,000 speeding fine', swissinfo.ch, 2010) and Euronews (2023-01-04, 'Finland's progressive punishment'): a 2010 motorist 'received 3,600 Swiss francs per day for 300 days -- that's more than a million euros in total' (CHF ~1.08M). ~USD 1.36M normalized to 2024 (CHF->USD x1.13 + inflation; USD figure is the collector's estimate).

homicide_intent.summary: England & Wales whole-life order (no fixed minimum term, effectively life with no release) applies to the most serious murders such as premeditated multiple murder or terrorist murder for offenders 21+.
England & Wales sets a 30-year minimum-term starting point for murders of particularly high seriousness (firearm/explosive, murder for gain, sexual/sadistic, two or more victims) for offenders 18+.
England & Wales sets a 25-year minimum-term starting point where the offender took a weapon to the scene intending to use it and did so, for offenders 18+ (offence on/after 2 Mar 2010).
homicide_intent.label_raw: Murder, 25-year minimum-term starting point (weapon taken to scene)

homicide_intent.summary: England & Wales applies a 15-year default minimum-term starting point for any other murder by an offender aged 18+ not falling within the higher paragraphs.
homicide_intent.source_citation: Sentencing Act 2020, Sch 21, para 5 (re-enacting Criminal Justice Act 2003 Sch 21) (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2020/17/schedule/21)

homicide_intent.source_citation: USSG 2A1.2; Sentencing Table level 38 CHC I = 235-293 mo (https://www.ussc.gov/guidelines/2025-guidelines-manual/annotated-2025-chapter-2-c; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Federal_Sentencing_Guidelines)

homicide_intent.label_raw: Involuntary manslaughter (reckless), USSG level 18, 27-33 mo at CHC I
homicide_intent.source_citation: USSG 2A1.4(a)(2); Sentencing Table level 18 CHC I = 27-33 mo; 18 U.S.C. 1112 (https://www.ussc.gov/guidelines/2025-guidelines-manual/annotated-2025-chapter-2-c)

homicide_intent.summary: US federal involuntary manslaughter (criminally negligent) carries USSG base offense level 12, mapping to 10-16 months (~0.83-1.33 years) at CHC I.

in_commonlaw.summary: Ireland murder (intentional killing or intent to cause serious injury) carries mandatory life imprisonment, with parole eligibility after 12 years and average time actually served on a life sentence of about 20 years.
in_commonlaw.harm_duration: ~20 years average time served (parole eligibility after 12 years)
in_commonlaw.source_citation: Criminal Justice Act 1990 (Ireland), s. 2; Parole Act 2019; Law Reform Commission Mandatory Sentences (LRC 108-2013); 'Life imprisonment in Ireland', https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_imprisonment_in_Ireland

in_commonlaw.summary: Ireland manslaughter (unlawful act or gross negligence, no intent to kill) has no mandatory minimum and a maximum of life, with a typical custodial range cited at roughly 4 to 15 years.
in_commonlaw.harm_duration: ~4 to 15 years (indicative typical custodial range; no formal guideline)
in_commonlaw.source_citation: Judicial Council Sentencing Guidelines & Information Committee materials, https://judicialcouncil.ie/assets/uploads/Sentence%20Information%20the%20General%20Public.pdf (practitioner/secondary characterization, indicative only)

in_commonlaw.summary: New Zealand murder (intentional, or reckless knowing death likely) carries a presumption of life imprisonment with a default minimum period of imprisonment of 10 years before parole.
in_commonlaw.harm_duration: 10 years (default minimum period of imprisonment before parole)

in_commonlaw.summary: New Zealand aggravated murder (s. 104 list, e.g. high brutality or multiple victims) requires a minimum non-parole period of 17 years unless manifestly unjust.
in_commonlaw.source_citation: Sentencing Act 2002 (NZ) s. 104; R v Williams [2005] 2 NZLR 506 (CA); https://www.legislation.govt.nz/act/public/2002/0009/latest/DLM136497.html

in_commonlaw.summary: New Zealand manslaughter (no murderous intent, unlawful act or gross negligence) has a maximum of life imprisonment but life is optional, with no statutory minimum and determinate terms usual.
in_commonlaw.harm_duration: no statutory minimum; determinate terms usual (max life)
in_commonlaw.source_citation: Crimes Act 1961 (NZ) s. 177; NZ Law Commission R139 ch. 11 'Sentencing for manslaughter', https://www.lawcom.govt.nz/sites/html-pubs/r139/Chapter+11+-+Sentencing+for+homicide/Sentencing+for+manslaughter.html

in_commonlaw.summary: India murder under IPC s. 302 (intent to kill, or intent to cause injury sufficient in the ordinary course to cause death) is punishable by death or life imprisonment plus fine, with life the standard and death reserved for the rarest of rare cases.
in_commonlaw.harm_duration: life imprisonment (or death penalty in rarest-of-rare cases)
in_commonlaw.label_raw: Murder, IPC s. 302 (re-enacted as BNS 2023 s. 103)
in_commonlaw.source_citation: Indian Penal Code 1860 s. 302; India Code https://www.indiacode.nic.in/; Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 s. 103; analysis https://thelegalschool.in/blog/difference-between-302-and-304-ipc

in_commonlaw.summary: India culpable homicide not amounting to murder under IPC s. 304 Part I (act done with intention or knowledge of likely death) is punishable by life imprisonment or up to 10 years plus fine.
in_commonlaw.harm_duration: life imprisonment, or up to 10 years (statutory maximum)
in_commonlaw.label_raw: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder, IPC s. 304 Part I (BNS 2023 s. 105)
in_commonlaw.source_citation: Indian Penal Code 1860 s. 304 Part I; https://www.indiacode.nic.in/show-data?actid=AC_CEN_5_23_00037_186045_1523266765688&orderno=341; BNS 2023 s. 105

in_commonlaw.summary: India culpable homicide not amounting to murder under IPC s. 304 Part II (knowledge act is likely to cause death but no intention) is punishable by up to 10 years imprisonment, or fine, or both.
in_commonlaw.harm_duration: up to 10 years (statutory maximum; no life)
in_commonlaw.label_raw: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder, IPC s. 304 Part II
in_commonlaw.source_citation: Indian Penal Code 1860 s. 304 Part II; https://www.indiacode.nic.in/show-data?actid=AC_CEN_5_23_00037_186045_1523266765688&orderno=341

in_commonlaw.summary: Scotland murder (intent to kill or wicked recklessness) carries mandatory life imprisonment, with an average punishment part of 20.5 years for life sentences in 2023-24.
in_commonlaw.harm_duration: 20.5 years average punishment part (parole floor) in 2023-24
in_commonlaw.label_raw: Murder, mandatory life with punishment part (Criminal Procedure (Scotland) Act 1995 s. 205)
in_commonlaw.source_citation: Criminal Procedure (Scotland) Act 1995 s. 205; Scottish Government, Criminal Proceedings in Scotland 2023-24, Appendix on punishment part of life sentences and OLRs, https://www.gov.scot/publications/criminal-proceedings-in-scotland-2023-24/pages/appendix-length-of-the-punishment-part-of-life-sentences-and-olrs/

in_commonlaw.summary: Scotland culpable homicide (lacks the wicked intent/recklessness of murder, analogous to manslaughter) attracts determinate terms, with 16 offenders receiving an average sentence of about 7 years (2,589 days) in 2021-22.
in_commonlaw.harm_duration: ~7 years (2,589 days) average determinate sentence in 2021-22
in_commonlaw.label_raw: Culpable homicide, determinate sentences (Scots common law)
in_commonlaw.source_citation: Scottish Government, Criminal Proceedings in Scotland 2021-22, custodial sentences by type of crime, https://www.gov.scot/publications/criminal-proceedings-scotland-2021-22/pages/13/

in_civillaw.summary: Germany StGB § 211 (Mord): intentional killing with statutory aggravators (base motives, treachery, cruelty) carries mandatory life imprisonment, parole eligible after a 15-year minimum (longer where particular gravity of guilt is found).
in_civillaw.source_citation: StGB § 211 (dejure.org/gesetze/StGB/211.html; gesetze-im-internet.de); summary: Murder in German law, Wikipedia. Premeditated/aggravated intentional killing; parole min 15 yr.

in_civillaw.summary: Germany StGB § 212 (Totschlag): intentional homicide without § 211 aggravators carries 5 to 15 years; especially grave cases → life, lesser cases under § 213 → 1 to 10 years.
in_civillaw.harm_duration: 5 to 15 years (life in especially grave cases)
in_civillaw.source_citation: StGB § 212 (dejure.org/gesetze/StGB/212.html). Range 5-15 yr; § 213 lesser cases 1-10 yr; especially grave → life.

in_civillaw.summary: Germany StGB § 222 (Fahrlässige Tötung): negligent homicide carries up to 5 years imprisonment or a fine.
in_civillaw.label_raw: Fahrlässige Tötung (§ 222 StGB) – up to 5 years or fine
in_civillaw.source_citation: StGB § 222 (gesetze-im-internet.de); summary: Murder in German law, Wikipedia. Up to 5 yr imprisonment or fine.

in_civillaw.summary: France Code pénal Art. 221-1 (Meurtre): intentional killing carries 30 years' criminal imprisonment (réclusion criminelle).
in_civillaw.source_citation: Légifrance, Code pénal Art. 221-1 (LEGIARTI000006417561). 30 yr réclusion criminelle.

in_civillaw.summary: France Code pénal Art. 221-3 (Assassinat): premeditated or ambush murder carries life imprisonment (réclusion criminelle à perpétuité).
in_civillaw.source_citation: Légifrance, Code pénal Section 1 Art. 221-1 to 221-5-4 (LEGISCTA000006165276). Premeditated/ambush intentional killing → life.

in_civillaw.summary: France Code pénal Art. 221-6 (Homicide involontaire): involuntary/negligent homicide carries up to 5 years plus a €75,000 fine, raised to 10 years plus €150,000 where committed with a deliberate breach of a safety obligation.
in_civillaw.harm_duration: up to 5 years (10 years with deliberate breach)
in_civillaw.label_raw: Homicide involontaire (Art. 221-6) – up to 5 yr + €75,000 (10 yr + €150,000 aggravated)
in_civillaw.source_citation: Légifrance, Code pénal Art. 221-6 (LEGIARTI000006417578). Up to 5 yr + €75,000 fine; 10 yr + €150,000 with manquement délibéré. Fine in original EUR; not USD-normalized.

in_civillaw.summary: Netherlands Wetboek van Strafrecht Art. 287 (Doodslag): intentional killing without premeditation (manslaughter) carries up to 25 years or a fifth-category fine.
in_civillaw.source_citation: Dutch Penal Code Art. 287; summary: Murder (Dutch law), Wikipedia. Up to 25 yr or 5th-category fine.

in_civillaw.summary: Netherlands Wetboek van Strafrecht Art. 289 (Moord): premeditated killing (murder) carries life imprisonment or a determinate term up to 30 years.
in_civillaw.label_raw: Moord (Art. 289 WvSr) – life or up to 30 years
in_civillaw.source_citation: Dutch Penal Code Art. 289; summary: Murder (Dutch law), Wikipedia. Premeditated intentional killing; life or determinate ≤ 30 yr.

in_civillaw.summary: Netherlands Wetboek van Strafrecht Art. 307 (Dood door schuld): death by negligence carries up to 2 years for ordinary negligence and up to 4 years for reckless/gross negligence (roekeloosheid).
in_civillaw.harm_duration: up to 2 years (up to 4 years if reckless/gross)
in_civillaw.label_raw: Dood door schuld (Art. 307 WvSr) – up to 2 yr (4 yr gross)
in_civillaw.source_citation: Dutch Penal Code Art. 307; summary: Murder (Dutch law), Wikipedia. Ordinary negligence ≤ 2 yr; reckless/gross negligence ≤ 4 yr.

in_civillaw.summary: Japan Penal Code Art. 199 (Satsujin): homicide/murder is punishable by death, life imprisonment with labour, or a definite term of not less than 5 years (up to the 20/30-year statutory cap).
in_civillaw.harm_duration: death, life, or 5 years to statutory cap (20/30 years)
in_civillaw.source_citation: Japanese Law Translation, Penal Code Art. 199 (japaneselawtranslation.go.jp/en/laws/view/3581/en). Act No. 45 of 1907, current translation. Death / life with labour / ≥ 5 yr.

in_civillaw.summary: Japan Penal Code Art. 210 (death due to negligence): punishable by a fine of up to ¥1,000,000, with no imprisonment as the base penalty.
in_civillaw.label_raw: Death due to negligence (Art. 210) – fine up to ¥1,000,000
in_civillaw.source_citation: Japanese Law Translation, Penal Code Art. 210 (japaneselawtranslation.go.jp/en/laws/view/3581/en). Fine ≤ ¥1,000,000, no base imprisonment. Fine in original JPY; not USD-normalized.

in_civillaw.summary: Japan Penal Code Art. 211 (negligence in pursuit of social activities / gross negligence causing death): punishable by imprisonment without work up to 5 years or a fine up to ¥2,500,000.
in_civillaw.label_raw: Gross/occupational negligence causing death (Art. 211) – ≤ 5 yr or ¥2,500,000
in_civillaw.source_citation: Japanese Law Translation, Penal Code Art. 211 (japaneselawtranslation.go.jp/en/laws/view/3581/en). Imprisonment without work ≤ 5 yr or fine ≤ ¥2,500,000. Fine in original JPY; not USD-normalized.

in_civillaw.summary: Sweden Brottsbalken Ch. 3 § 1 (Mord): intentional killing (murder) carries a fixed term of 10 to 18 years or life.
in_civillaw.label_raw: Mord (Brottsbalken Ch.3 §1) – 10 to 18 years or life
in_civillaw.source_citation: Brottsbalken Ch. 3 § 1; summary: Murder in Swedish law, Wikipedia. Fixed 10-18 yr or life.

in_civillaw.summary: Sweden Brottsbalken Ch. 3 § 2 (Dråp): less-serious intentional killing (manslaughter) carries 6 to 10 years.
in_civillaw.source_citation: Brottsbalken Ch. 3 § 2; summary: Murder in Swedish law, Wikipedia. 6-10 yr.

in_civillaw.summary: Sweden Brottsbalken Ch. 3 § 3 (Vållande till annans död): negligent homicide carries day-fines (petty cases) up to 2 years imprisonment, with the gross (grovt) variant 1 to 6 years.
in_civillaw.harm_duration: up to 2 years (1 to 6 years if gross)
in_civillaw.label_raw: Vållande till annans död (Brottsbalken Ch.3 §3) – day-fines to 2 yr (gross 1-6 yr)
in_civillaw.source_citation: Brottsbalken Ch. 3 § 3; summary: Murder in Swedish law, Wikipedia. Base: day-fines to ≤ 2 yr; grovt 1-6 yr.

Face value ¥226.07M ÷ 151.353 IRS 2024 avg JPY/USD ≈ USD 1.49M; escalated to 2024 (~¥250M) ≈ USD 1.65M. https://www8.cao.go.jp/koutu/chou-ken/19html/houkoku.html ; https://www.mlit.go.jp/tec/hyouka/public/pdf_kentoukai03/04.pdf

vsl_intl.summary: An academic stated-preference choice experiment puts Japan's Value of Statistical Life at JPY 350 million in 2002 yen, roughly USD 2.31 million in 2024 dollars, an upper-bound cross-check above the Cabinet Office figure.
vsl_intl.source_citation: Japanese choice-experiment / stated-preference literature as summarized in OECD, Mortality Risk Valuation in Environment, Health and Transport Policies (2012) (VSL ¥350M in 2002 yen, ≈ US$2.9M at 2002 rates); nominal ¥350M ÷ 151.353 IRS 2024 avg JPY/USD ≈ USD 2.31M. https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/publications/reports/2012/02/mortality-risk-valuation-in-environment-health-and-transport-policies_g1g1690a/9789264130807-en.pdf ; JSCE meta-analysis https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jscejj/79/20/79_23-20008/_article/-char/en

qaly_intl.summary: Canada's CADTH applies a de facto willingness-to-pay threshold of ~50,000 CAD/QALY (~36,500 USD in 2024) as the operative cost-effectiveness anchor for drug reimbursement.
qaly_intl.source_citation: Skedgel et al., 'The impact of willingness-to-pay threshold on price reduction recommendations for oncology drugs: a review of CADTH assessments,' PubMed 38567953 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38567953/); Value in Health, 'CADTH's $50,000 Cost-Effectiveness Threshold: Fact or Fiction?' (https://www.valueinhealthjournal.com/article/S1098-3015(16)32187-8/fulltext). Original 50,000 CAD nominal (~2021-2022) x 0.73 USD/CAD = ~36,500 USD (2024).

qaly_intl.summary: Australia's PBAC uses an implicit ~50,000 AUD/QALY rule-of-thumb (~33,000 USD in 2024), with an empirical recommend/reject band spanning roughly 42,000-76,000 AUD/LY.
qaly_intl.source_citation: Australian Prescriber, 'Economic evaluation of medicines' (https://australianprescriber.tg.org.au/articles/economic-evaluation-of-medicines.html); Wang et al., comparing ICERs to NICE/PBAC, ScienceDirect S1098301518302031 (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1098301518302031). Original ~50,000 AUD nominal x 0.66 USD/AUD = ~33,000 USD; rejection ~76,000 AUD/LY (~49,500 USD), near-certain accept ~42,000 AUD/LY (~27,700 USD).

qaly_intl.summary: Germany's IQWiG explicitly rejects any universal cost-per-QALY willingness-to-pay threshold, instead using an indication-specific efficiency-frontier method, so it supplies no single $/QALY anchor.
qaly_intl.source_citation: Caro & Nord et al., 'The efficiency frontier approach to economic evaluation of health-care interventions,' ResearchGate 44699342 (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/44699342_The_efficiency_frontier_approach_to_economic_evaluation_of_health-care_interventions); Gandjour 2015, Int J Health Plann Manage (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/hpm.2247). Structural caveat: Germany provides no single anchor number.

qaly_intl.summary: The Netherlands' Zorginstituut sets severity-tiered WTP reference values of 20,000/50,000/80,000 EUR/QALY by proportional shortfall, with the most-severe top tier of 80,000 EUR/QALY (~86,400 USD in 2024).
qaly_intl.label_raw: Netherlands (ZIN) top tier 80,000 EUR/QALY; tiers 20,000/50,000/80,000 EUR
qaly_intl.source_citation: Reckers-Droog et al. / 'Varying Willingness to Pay Based on Severity of Illness... Netherlands,' Value in Health S1098-3015(21)01690-9 (https://www.valueinhealthjournal.com/article/S1098-3015(21)01690-9/fulltext). Established 2015; PS 0.10-0.40=20,000 EUR (~21,600 USD), PS 0.41-0.70=50,000 EUR (~54,000 USD), PS 0.71-1.00=80,000 EUR (~86,400 USD) at 1.08 USD/EUR. Top tier used as anchor value.

qaly_intl.summary: Sweden's TLV applies severity-tiered implied WTP up to ~750,000 SEK/QALY (high, ~70,500 USD) and ~1,000,000 SEK/QALY (very high, ~94,000 USD in 2024), with no statutory threshold and >2M SEK/QALY accepted for rare+severe cases.
qaly_intl.source_citation: Svensson et al., 'Reimbursement Decisions for Pharmaceuticals in Sweden: Impact of Disease Severity and Cost Effectiveness,' PharmacoEconomics (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40273-015-0307-6); Quantify Research, 'How much is TLV willing to pay for a QALY in Sweden?' (2024) (https://quantifyresearch.com/2024/01/31/how-much-is-tlv-willing-to-pay-for-a-qaly-in-sweden/). Tiers at 0.094 USD/SEK: low 200k-250k (~19,000-23,500 USD), medium 500k-600k (~47,000-56,000 USD), high 750k (~70,500 USD), very high 1,000,000 (~94,000 USD). Very-high tier used as anchor value.

qaly_intl.summary: Thailand's HITAP uses an explicit national WTP threshold of 160,000 THB/QALY (~4,560 USD in 2024, ~1.3x GDP per capita), above which ICERs trigger price negotiation.
qaly_intl.source_citation: OHE, 'Around the World in HTAs: Thailand' (https://www.ohe.org/insights/around-the-world-in-htas-thailand/); Teerawattananon et al. / HITAP empirical study, ScienceDirect S221188372400090X (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S221188372400090X). Set 2013 (raised stepwise 100k pre-2010 -> 120k 2010 -> 160k 2013); 160,000 THB x 0.0285 USD/THB = ~4,560 USD (2024).

qaly_intl.summary: The WHO-CHOICE / Commission on Macroeconomics and Health rule (2001) judged interventions cost-effective at 1x-3x GDP per capita per DALY averted, a generic global benchmark now deprecated as never rigorously derived.
qaly_intl.label_raw: WHO-CHOICE / CMH 1x-3x GDP per capita per DALY (deprecated)
qaly_intl.source_citation: Bertram et al., 'Understanding and improving the one and three times GDP per capita cost-effectiveness thresholds,' Health Policy and Planning 32(1):141 (https://academic.oup.com/heapol/article/32/1/141/2555408); WHO Bulletin, 'Thresholds for the cost-effectiveness of interventions: alternative approaches' (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4339959/). Multiplier of GDP/capita, not a fixed figure: at ~13,300 USD 2024 world GDP/capita, 1x-3x ~= 13,300-40,000 USD/DALY; LMIC like Thailand (~7,000 USD GDP/capita) 1x ~= 7,000 USD. money_value_usd2024 null because it scales with GDP per capita. Deprecated as a hard threshold.

qaly_intl.summary: Excluding the deprecated WHO multiplier and Germany's no-threshold method, the standard non-severity-adjusted cross-jurisdiction WTP-for-one-QALY midpoint sits at roughly 33,000-50,000 USD/QALY, with severity-weighted ceilings reaching ~86,000-94,000 USD/QALY.
qaly_intl.label_raw: Cross-jurisdiction standard QALY midpoint ~33,000-50,000 USD; ceilings ~86,000-94,000 USD
qaly_intl.source_citation: Calibration note synthesized from the qaly_intl jurisdiction set: high-income single-QALY anchors cluster as Thailand ~4,600; Australia ~33,000; Canada ~36,500; Netherlands ~22,000-86,000 (severity-scaled); Sweden ~19,000-94,000 (severity-scaled). Midpoint of the standard band (33,000-50,000) = ~41,500 USD used as money_value_usd2024.

liberty_dur.summary: Germany's StGB §239(3) raises the punishment range to 1-10 years when unlawful deprivation of liberty exceeds exactly one week, giving an explicit legislative step function for detention duration.
liberty_dur.label_raw: Germany — §239(3) StGB statutory threshold (deprivation of liberty > 1 week)
liberty_dur.source_citation: Strafgesetzbuch (StGB) §239(3), text "länger als eine Woche"; https://dejure.org/gesetze/StGB/239.html and official English at https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/englisch_stgb/englisch_stgb.html (aggravated range 1-10 yrs triggered by confinement exceeding one week; §239(4) not under 3 yrs if victim dies).

liberty_dur.summary: Germany's StGB §239(1) basic offence punishes unlawful confinement of any short duration (hours to days, below the 1-week threshold) with up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine, serving as the sub-week lower-bound anchor.
liberty_dur.source_citation: Strafgesetzbuch (StGB) §239(1) (up to 5 years or fine, no duration floor); https://dejure.org/gesetze/StGB/239.html — lower-bound anchor distinguishing sub-week from over-week confinement.

liberty_dur.summary: In State v. William Mozingo Jr. (Summit County, Ohio, 2024) the defendant held victim Chloe Jones hostage in a garage for 4 days and received an indefinite 25 to 31.5 year sentence, aggravated by violence/assault.
liberty_dur.label_raw: USA (Ohio) — State v. William Mozingo Jr., Summit County (Akron)
liberty_dur.source_citation: State v. William Mozingo Jr., Summit County (Akron), Ohio, sentenced 2024; indefinite 25-31.5 yr sentence (deliberate abduction + assault with baseball bat). https://myfox28columbus.com/amp/news/nation-world/william-mozingo-junior-serial-kidnapper-held-ohio-woman-hostage-beat-her-baseball-bat-learns-his-fate-conviction-cincinnati-kidnapping-high-profile-court-cases-verdict-summit-county-assault (penalty blended with violence/assault).

liberty_dur.summary: In United States v. Brian David Mitchell (D. Utah, 2011), the kidnapping and sexual assault of 14-year-old Elizabeth Smart over ~9 months (June 2002-March 2003) drew two consecutive life sentences without parole.
liberty_dur.label_raw: USA (federal) — United States v. Brian David Mitchell (Elizabeth Smart kidnapping)
liberty_dur.source_citation: United States v. Brian David Mitchell, D. Utah, sentenced 2011; two life sentences no parole (abducted 5 Jun 2002, recovered ~12 Mar 2003; kidnapping + sexual assault of a minor). FBI press release https://archives.fbi.gov/archives/saltlakecity/press-releases/2011/slc052511a.htm ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidnapping_of_Elizabeth_Smart (penalty blended with sexual assault; life sentence = saturation, jail-years not numerically expressible).

liberty_dur.summary: In State v. Ariel Castro (Ohio, 2013) the captivity of three women for roughly 9-11 years each, compounded with rape and aggravated murder of a fetus, drew life without parole plus 1,000 years and a $100,000 fine.
liberty_dur.label_raw: USA (Ohio) — State v. Ariel Castro (Cleveland kidnappings)
liberty_dur.source_citation: State v. Ariel Castro, Ohio, sentenced 2013; life without parole + 1,000 years + $100,000 fine (~$135k in 2024 USD); pleaded to 937 counts incl. kidnapping, rape, aggravated murder of a fetus. Victims: Michelle Knight ~11 yrs (from Aug 2002), Amanda Berry ~10 yrs (Apr 2003), Gina DeJesus ~9 yrs (Apr 2004), all rescued 6 May 2013. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariel_Castro_kidnappings — extreme outlier; multi-year confinement compounded with rape/murder; upper-bound saturation point, not a clean per-time ratio.

liberty_dur.summary: California Penal Code §§236/237 punishes felony false imprisonment by violence, menace, fraud, or deceit on a 16-month/2-year/3-year triad with no minimum detention period, providing a statutory liberty-deprivation anchor.
liberty_dur.harm_duration: any (statute states no minimum period; restraint can be brief)
liberty_dur.label_raw: USA (California) — Penal Code §§236/237 statutory anchor (felony false imprisonment by violence/menace/fraud/deceit)
liberty_dur.source_citation: California Penal Code §§236-237 (felony triad 16 mo / 2 yr / 3 yr; misdemeanor up to 1 yr county jail; elderly/dependent-adult victim up to 4 yr, 5 if injury). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PEN&sectionNum=236 — statute states no minimum period (restraint can be brief).

liberty_dur.summary: The England & Wales Sentencing Council kidnap/false imprisonment guideline treats a prolonged captivity period as a High culpability factor (range up to 16 years, statutory max life), with a 2022 immediate-custody average of 5 years 9 months.
liberty_dur.harm_duration: prolonged period (High culpability factor; duration is a culpability multiplier, not a fixed per-time rate)
liberty_dur.label_raw: UK (England & Wales) — Kidnap/False Imprisonment Sentencing Guideline (Sentencing Council)
liberty_dur.source_citation: Sentencing Council Kidnap/False Imprisonment guideline (offence range community order up to 16 yrs; statutory max life; "victim held captive over a prolonged period" is a High culpability factor; 2022 immediate-custody average custodial sentence length 5 yrs 9 mo post guilty-plea). https://sentencingcouncil.org.uk/guidelines/kidnap-false-imprisonment/ — duration is a culpability multiplier rather than a fixed per-time rate.

liberty_dur.summary: In R v Amanda Wixon (Gloucestershire Crown Court, 2026) the victim was held captive for over 20 years (since 1996, discovered March 2021) yet the false-imprisonment-plus-forced-labour sentence was 13 years, illustrating strongly sub-linear scaling.
liberty_dur.label_raw: UK (England & Wales) — R v Amanda Wixon, Gloucestershire Crown Court
liberty_dur.source_citation: R v Amanda Wixon, Gloucestershire Crown Court, sentenced 2026; 13 years (1 count false imprisonment + 2 counts forced/compulsory labour + 3 counts assault); victim held captive since 1996, discovered March 2021. CPS https://www.cps.gov.uk/south-west/news/gloucestershire-woman-who-imprisoned-victim-over-20-years-jailed — illustrates strong sub-linear scaling (20+ yrs deprivation -> 13 yrs custody).

liberty_dur.summary: In a Sheffield Crown Court trafficking/false imprisonment case (2023) two men chained to radiators and starved for just under two weeks led to sentences of nearly 20 years each, reflecting a high penalty-per-time due to torture-like aggravation.
liberty_dur.label_raw: UK (England & Wales) — Sheffield Crown Court trafficking/false imprisonment case (two defendants)
liberty_dur.source_citation: Sheffield Crown Court trafficking/false imprisonment case, 2023; nearly 20 years each (two Albanian men chained to radiators, starved). https://www.thestar.co.uk/news/crime/sheffield-crown-court-men-jailed-for-nearly-20-years-following-deeply-disturbing-false-imprisonment-case-3973189 — high penalty-per-time because aggravated by torture-like conditions (forced labour, violence, starvation); must be isolated from pure liberty_time.

liberty_dur.summary: Canada's Criminal Code s.279(2) forcible/unlawful confinement carries a maximum of 10 years on indictment (18 months summary) with no stated minimum detention period, providing a federal statutory liberty-deprivation anchor.
liberty_dur.label_raw: Canada — Criminal Code s.279(2) forcible/unlawful confinement statutory anchor
liberty_dur.source_citation: Criminal Code (Canada) s.279(2) (max 10 yrs on indictment / max 18 mo summary); s.279(1) kidnapping with aggravating factors mandatory minimum 5 yrs (7 with priors), max life. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/c-46/section-279.html — no stated minimum period.

liberty_dur.summary: In R v Mills (1998, BC CA) a kidnapping in which the victim was driven around for several hours drew sentences of roughly 4 to 5 years, showing that even brief detentions attract multi-year custody.
liberty_dur.label_raw: Canada — R v Mills, 1998 CanLII 15020 (BC CA)
liberty_dur.source_citation: R v Mills, 1998 CanLII 15020 (BC CA); 4-5 yrs (co-accused Babin 4 yrs; Mills ~5 yrs) for kidnapping, victim driven around several hours. Criminal Law Notebook, https://criminalnotebook.ca/index.php/Kidnapping_and_Unlawful_Confinement_(Sentencing_Cases) — short detention drawing multi-year sentence (sub-linear scaling reference).

liberty_dur.summary: Under NSW Crimes Act 1900 s.86 (detain for advantage/kidnapping, basic max 14 years; 25 years if in company or with wounding/GBH), the cited R v Kerr involved detention under threat of violence for around 36 hours.
liberty_dur.label_raw: Australia (NSW) — Crimes Act 1900 s.86 statutory anchor + R v Kerr
liberty_dur.source_citation: NSW Crimes Act 1900 s.86 (basic s.86(1) max 14 yrs; 25 yrs if in company per s.86(2)/86A or with wounding/GBH); R v Kerr cited in NSW Judicial Commission Sentencing Bench Book (victim detained under threat of violence around 36 hours). https://www.judcom.nsw.gov.au/publications/benchbks/sentencing/kidnapping.html — penalty_jail_years recorded as basic statutory max (14 yrs).

diyya_blood_money.summary: Saudi Arabia (Hanbali) standard diyya for accidental/wrongful death of a Muslim man is SAR 300,000 (~$80,000), a statutory restitution transfer to the victim's family pegged to ~100 adult camels (not a willingness-to-pay life value).
diyya_blood_money.label_raw: Full diyya, accidental death, Muslim man, SAR 300,000
diyya_blood_money.source_citation: Life in Saudi Arabia, Blood money (Diyyah) and its calculation, https://lifeinsaudiarabia.net/blood-money-diyyah-and-its-calculation/; Wikipedia, Blood money in Islam, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_money_in_Islam

diyya_blood_money.summary: Saudi Arabia: intentional murder has no statutory diyya ceiling — the victim's family may demand any amount or qisas (execution), so the price to avoid retaliation is uncapped (severity-ladder anchor rather than a fixed compensation figure).
diyya_blood_money.label_raw: Intentional murder: no diyya ceiling; family may demand any amount or qisas
diyya_blood_money.source_citation: Wikipedia, Blood money in Islam, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_money_in_Islam

diyya_blood_money.summary: Saudi Arabia: a Muslim woman's diyya is half a man's (SAR 150,000, ~$40,000) — an identity (gender) multiplier of 0.5 applied to the whole compensation schedule, a non-universal divergence axis.
diyya_blood_money.label_raw: Muslim woman = 1/2 of man, SAR 150,000
diyya_blood_money.source_citation: Money Jihad compilation, https://moneyjihad.wordpress.com/2011/10/14/islam-prices-people-like-livestock/; Wikipedia, Blood money in Islam, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_money_in_Islam

diyya_blood_money.summary: Saudi Arabia: a Christian/Jewish ('People of the Book') man's diyya is half a Muslim man's (SAR 150,000, ~$40,000) — a religion-based identity multiplier of 0.5 on the compensation schedule.
diyya_blood_money.label_raw: Christian/Jewish man = 1/2 of Muslim man
diyya_blood_money.source_citation: Wikipedia, Blood money in Islam, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_money_in_Islam

diyya_blood_money.summary: Saudi Arabia: a Hindu/other non-Muslim man's diyya is 1/16 of a Muslim man's (~SAR 6,666, ~$1,778) — the steepest religion-based identity multiplier (0.0625) on the compensation schedule.
diyya_blood_money.label_raw: Hindu/other non-Muslim man = 1/16 of Muslim man (~SAR 6,666)
diyya_blood_money.source_citation: Wikipedia, Blood money in Islam, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_money_in_Islam

diyya_blood_money.summary: Iran (Twelver Shia) full diyya for a Muslim man in non-sacred months, year 1404, is 16 billion rials (~$27,000 at open-market rate ~600,000 IRR/USD); +1/3 during the four sacred lunar months — a judiciary-decreed restitution transfer, not a VSL.
diyya_blood_money.label_raw: Full diyya Muslim man, 16,000,000,000 IRR, non-sacred months, year 1404
diyya_blood_money.source_citation: Nour Law Offices, Diya (blood money) applicable in Iranian year 1404, judiciary decree No. 100/73552/9000 (12 Mar 2025), https://nourlaw.com/diya-blood-money-applicable-in-the-current-iranian-year-1404-21-march-2025-19-march-2026/

diyya_blood_money.summary: Iran: a woman's offender-borne diyya is half a man's (~$13,500), though a May 2019 Supreme Court ruling has the state Fund for Bodily Injuries cover the other half so the family's paid-out total equalizes — the priced value of a woman's life to the offender remains a 0.5 identity multiplier.
diyya_blood_money.label_raw: Woman's diyya = 1/2 of man's (offender pays half; state fund covers remainder)
diyya_blood_money.source_citation: Center for Human Rights in Iran, Blood money paid for a woman in Iran is still half that paid for a man (Aug 2019), https://iranhumanrights.org/2019/08/blood-money-paid-for-a-woman-in-iran-is-still-half-that-paid-for-a-man-despite-new-ruling/

diyya_blood_money.summary: UAE federal diyya for wrongful/accidental death is AED 200,000 (~$54,500), fixed by Federal Law No. 9 of 2003 and applied uniformly to male or female (no gender differential in the statutory amount); the 2026 Civil Code Art. 259 lets courts add material/moral damages beyond diyya.
diyya_blood_money.label_raw: Diyya AED 200,000, Federal Law No. 9 of 2003, gender-uniform
diyya_blood_money.source_citation: Ask The Law UAE, Blood money compensation (Diya) in UAE, https://askthelaw.ae/legal-articles/miscellaneous/blood-money-compensation-diya-in-uae/; Khaleej Times, Shariah and body-parts compensation, https://www.khaleejtimes.com/uae/shariah-and-body-parts-compensation

diyya_blood_money.summary: Qatar diyya is fixed at QAR 200,000 per deceased (~$55,000), explicitly uniform regardless of gender, residency, or religion (male/female, citizen/resident, Muslim/non-Muslim all equal) under Penal Code Law No. 11 of 2004 — a system that rejects identity multipliers.
diyya_blood_money.label_raw: Diyya QAR 200,000, uniform across gender/residency/religion, Law No. 11 of 2004
diyya_blood_money.source_citation: Fatima Al Naimi Law, Traffic accidents in Qatar: compensation and blood money (Diya), https://fatimaalnaimi.qa/traffic-accidents-in-qatar-compensation-and-blood-money-diya/

diyya_blood_money.summary: Kuwait full diyya was KWD 10,000 (~$32,500) under Decree-Law No. 67 of 1980, unchanged for about four decades — a long-static statutory restitution floor.
diyya_blood_money.label_raw: Diyya KWD 10,000, Decree-Law No. 67 of 1980
diyya_blood_money.source_citation: Gulf News, Kuwait doubles blood money from 10,000 to 20,000 dinars and abolishes gender-discriminatory law, https://gulfnews.com/world/gulf/kuwait/kuwait-doubles-blood-money-from-10000-to-20000-dinarsand-abolishes-gender-discriminatory-law-1.500063735

diyya_blood_money.summary: Kuwait doubled diyya to KWD 20,000 (~$65,000) in 2025 and the new decree-law abolished the gender differential (women's diyya equalized to men's) — a case of a sharia system dropping the identity multiplier.
diyya_blood_money.label_raw: Diyya doubled to KWD 20,000 (2025); gender differential abolished
diyya_blood_money.source_citation: Gulf News, Kuwait doubles blood money and abolishes gender-discriminatory law, https://gulfnews.com/world/gulf/kuwait/kuwait-doubles-blood-money-from-10000-to-20000-dinarsand-abolishes-gender-discriminatory-law-1.500063735; Arab Times, Kuwait increases blood money value to 20,000 dinars, https://www.arabtimesonline.com/news/kuwait-increases-blood-money-value-to-20000-dinars-with-new-decree-law/

diyya_blood_money.summary: Pakistan diyat for FY 2024-25 is PKR 8,103,955 (~$29,000), set by the Ministry of Finance pegged to 30,630 grams of silver (floats with the silver market, up 20% from FY2023-24) under Penal Code s.323, and applied equally to Muslims and non-Muslims.
diyya_blood_money.label_raw: Diyat PKR 8,103,955 (FY2024-25), pegged to 30,630 g silver, religion-uniform
diyya_blood_money.source_citation: ARY News, Pakistan fixes new diyat amount for 2024-25, https://arynews.tv/pakistan-fixes-new-diyat-amount-for-2024-25/; Dawn, https://www.dawn.com/news/1863172

diyya_blood_money.summary: Northern Nigeria sharia states (Maliki; e.g. Zamfara, Kano) set homicide diyya at 100 camels or local-market monetary equivalent payable to the victim's heirs as the alternative to qisas — codes specify the camel-count standard rather than a fixed indexed naira sum.
diyya_blood_money.label_raw: Homicide diyya = 100 camels or monetary equivalent; alternative to qisas
diyya_blood_money.source_citation: Grokipedia, Sharia in Nigeria, https://grokipedia.com/page/Sharia_in_Nigeria; USCIRF, Shari'ah Criminal Law in Northern Nigeria, https://www.uscirf.gov/sites/default/files/USCIRF_ShariahLawinNigeria_report_120919%20v3R.pdf

diyya_blood_money.summary: Classical arsh schedule: loss of both eyes, both hands, both feet, nose, tongue, male genitalia, or both ears each = full diyya (100 camels = 1x a life), encoding paired-organ loss as equivalent to death in compensation terms across Sunni, Twelver Shia, and the GCC/Nigeria statutes.
diyya_blood_money.jurisdiction: Sharia jurisdictions (cross-system: Sunni schools, Twelver Shia/Iran, UAE/Qatar/Nigeria)
diyya_blood_money.label_raw: Both eyes/hands/feet/nose/tongue/genitalia/both ears = full diyya
diyya_blood_money.source_citation: Malik's Muwatta, Book 43 (Blood-Money), https://www.iium.edu.my/deed/hadith/malik/043_mmt.html; Khaleej Times, Shariah and body-parts compensation, https://www.khaleejtimes.com/uae/shariah-and-body-parts-compensation

diyya_blood_money.summary: Arsh for loss of one eye = 1/2 diyya (50 camels), codified in the UAE as AED 100,000 (~$27,250) — pricing one eye at half a human life, a ratio invariant across Sunni and Shia codes.
diyya_blood_money.label_raw: One eye = 1/2 diyya (50 camels); UAE AED 100,000
diyya_blood_money.source_citation: Khaleej Times, Shariah and body-parts compensation, https://www.khaleejtimes.com/uae/shariah-and-body-parts-compensation; Malik's Muwatta, Book 43, https://www.iium.edu.my/deed/hadith/malik/043_mmt.html

diyya_blood_money.summary: Arsh for loss of one hand = 1/2 diyya (50 camels), codified in the UAE as AED 100,000 (~$27,250); both hands = full diyya — pricing one hand at half a human life.
diyya_blood_money.label_raw: One hand = 1/2 diyya (50 camels); UAE AED 100,000

diyya_blood_money.label_raw: One foot/leg = 1/2 diyya (50 camels)

diyya_blood_money.summary: Arsh for loss of one ear = 1/2 diyya, codified in the UAE as AED 100,000 (~$27,250); both ears = full diyya — pricing one ear at half a human life.
diyya_blood_money.label_raw: One ear = 1/2 diyya; UAE AED 100,000
diyya_blood_money.source_citation: Khaleej Times, Shariah and body-parts compensation, https://www.khaleejtimes.com/uae/shariah-and-body-parts-compensation

diyya_blood_money.summary: Arsh for loss of one finger (or one toe) = 1/10 diyya (10 camels), UAE equivalent ~AED 20,000 (~$5,450) — pricing a finger at one-tenth of a human life, a ratio invariant across Sunni and Shia codes.
