diyya_blood_money.label_raw: One finger joint = 1/3 of a finger's diyya (~3.33 camels, ~1/30 life)
diyya_blood_money.source_citation: Malik's Muwatta, Book 43 (Blood-Money), https://www.iium.edu.my/deed/hadith/malik/043_mmt.html

diyya_blood_money.summary: Arsh for loss of one tooth = 1/20 diyya (5 camels), with the UAE applying a 5-camel equivalent per tooth — pricing a tooth at one-twentieth of a human life, invariant across Sunni and Shia codes.
diyya_blood_money.label_raw: One tooth = 1/20 diyya (5 camels)
diyya_blood_money.source_citation: Malik's Muwatta, Book 43 (Blood-Money), https://www.iium.edu.my/deed/hadith/malik/043_mmt.html; Khaleej Times, Shariah and body-parts compensation, https://www.khaleejtimes.com/uae/shariah-and-body-parts-compensation

homicide_diverse.summary: China PRC Criminal Law Art. 232 punishes intentional homicide by death, life, or fixed term >=10 years (3-10 years if circumstances relatively minor); a custodial/capital construct, not monetary compensation.
homicide_diverse.label_raw: Intentional homicide (Art. 232): death, life, or fixed-term >=10 years; 3-10 years if circumstances relatively minor

homicide_diverse.summary: China PRC Criminal Law Art. 233 punishes negligently causing death by 3-7 years (<=3 years if minor); a custodial construct whose 7-year cap sits below the intentional 10-year floor, giving a within-jurisdiction intent ratio of ~3.3x.
homicide_diverse.label_raw: Negligently causing death (Art. 233): 3-7 years; <=3 years if circumstances minor

homicide_diverse.summary: Russia Criminal Code Art. 105 s1 punishes simple murder by 6-15 years; a custodial construct forming the intentional anchor against negligent Art. 109.
homicide_diverse.source_citation: Russia, Criminal Code No. 63-FZ Art. 105 s1 (Wikipedia: Murder in Russian law)

homicide_diverse.summary: Russia Criminal Code Art. 105 s2 punishes aggravated murder by 8-20 years, life, or death (death under standing moratorium since 1996/1999); a custodial/capital construct reserving the unbounded tail for intentional killing.
homicide_diverse.label_raw: Murder, aggravated (Art. 105 s2): 8-20 years, life, or death (death penalty under moratorium)
homicide_diverse.source_citation: Russia, Criminal Code No. 63-FZ Art. 105 s2 (Wikipedia: Murder in Russian law)

homicide_diverse.summary: Russia Criminal Code Art. 109 punishes causing death by negligence at up to 2 years (3 if via professional duty breach, 4 if >=2 victims); a custodial construct yielding a ~3x intent ratio against simple murder's 6-year floor.
homicide_diverse.label_raw: Causing death by negligence (Art. 109): up to 2 years; up to 3 if professional duty breach; up to 4 if >=2 victims
homicide_diverse.source_citation: Russia, Criminal Code No. 63-FZ Art. 109 (legal-tools.org PDF); sub-tiers from secondary summaries

homicide_diverse.summary: Brazil Codigo Penal Art. 121 caput punishes homicidio doloso by 6-20 years reclusao; a custodial construct, no death penalty for ordinary homicide.
homicide_diverse.label_raw: Intentional homicide / homicidio doloso (Art. 121 caput): 6-20 years reclusao
homicide_diverse.source_citation: Brazil, Codigo Penal Decreto-Lei 2.848/1940 Art. 121 caput (jurishand.com; Wikipedia: Murder in Brazilian law)

homicide_diverse.summary: Brazil Codigo Penal Art. 121 s3 punishes homicidio culposo by 1-3 years detencao (+1/3 for professional-rule breach or failure to render aid); a custodial construct giving a clean bounded intent ratio of ~6-6.7x.
homicide_diverse.label_raw: Negligent homicide / homicidio culposo (Art. 121 s3): 1-3 years detencao; +1/3 for professional breach or failure to aid
homicide_diverse.source_citation: Brazil, Codigo Penal Decreto-Lei 2.848/1940 Art. 121 s3 (jurishand.com)

homicide_diverse.summary: Nigeria (Southern states) Criminal Code Act s. 319 imposes a mandatory death sentence for murder (under-17 offenders detained during the Governor's pleasure); a capital construct, the intentional anchor.
homicide_diverse.label_raw: Murder (s. 319): mandatory death sentence; under-17 detained during Governor's pleasure
homicide_diverse.source_citation: Nigeria, Criminal Code Act Cap. C38 s. 319 (jurist.ng/criminal_code_act/sec-319)

homicide_diverse.summary: Nigeria (Southern states) Criminal Code Act s. 325 (defined s. 317) makes manslaughter liable to life imprisonment with court discretion to impose less; a custodial construct bundling reckless/negligent killing without a low fixed cap, so the intent multiplier is effectively unbounded against the mandatory death tier.
homicide_diverse.label_raw: Manslaughter (s. 325, defined s. 317): liable to life imprisonment, court discretion to impose less
homicide_diverse.source_citation: Nigeria, Criminal Code Act Cap. C38 ss. 317/325 (jurist.ng/criminal_code_act/sec-317, sec-325)

homicide_diverse.summary: Nigeria (Northern states) Penal Code s. 221 punishes culpable homicide punishable with death by death; a capital construct with an Islamic-law overlay, the intentional anchor.
homicide_diverse.label_raw: Culpable homicide punishable with death (s. 221): death
homicide_diverse.source_citation: Nigeria (North), Penal Code (Northern States) Federal Provisions Act 1959 s. 221 (ilga.org PDF)

homicide_diverse.summary: Nigeria (Northern states) Penal Code s. 224 punishes culpable homicide not punishable with death (covering rash/negligent acts per s. 220(c)) by life or any lesser term plus possible fine; a custodial construct with Islamic-law overlay, unbounded intent tail against the death tier.
homicide_diverse.label_raw: Culpable homicide NOT punishable with death (s. 224, covers rash/negligent acts s. 220(c)): life imprisonment or any lesser term, plus possible fine
homicide_diverse.source_citation: Nigeria (North), Penal Code (Northern States) Federal Provisions Act 1959 ss. 224/220 (Mondaq: Murder, Culpable Homicide in Nigeria)

homicide_diverse.summary: Indonesia KUHP Art. 338 punishes pembunuhan (murder) by a maximum 15 years; a custodial construct, the middle tier of a three-level intent ladder.
homicide_diverse.source_citation: Indonesia, KUHP / Penal Code 1918 Art. 338 (icnl.org KUHP English)

homicide_diverse.summary: Indonesia KUHP Art. 340 punishes pembunuhan berencana (premeditated murder) by death, life, or up to 20 years; a custodial/capital construct escalating intentional killing to a premeditated top tier.
homicide_diverse.label_raw: Premeditated murder / pembunuhan berencana (Art. 340): death, life, or up to 20 years

homicide_diverse.summary: Indonesia KUHP Art. 359 punishes negligence causing death by a maximum 5 years (or 1 year detention); a custodial construct giving a ~3x intent ratio against plain murder's 15-year cap.
homicide_diverse.label_raw: Negligence causing death (Art. 359): max 5 years (or 1 year detention)

homicide_diverse.summary: Mexico Codigo Penal Federal Arts. 302+307 punish homicidio doloso simple by 12-24 years; a custodial construct, no death penalty (abolished 2005), the intentional anchor.
homicide_diverse.label_raw: Intentional homicide / homicidio doloso simple (Arts. 302+307): 12-24 years
homicide_diverse.source_citation: Mexico, Codigo Penal Federal Arts. 302+307 (Justia Mexico Arts. 302-309)

homicide_diverse.summary: Mexico Codigo Penal Federal Art. 60 caps culpa-based penalties at 1/4 of the corresponding intentional penalty (roughly ~3-6 years for basic homicidio culposo); a custodial construct that structurally fixes the intent multiplier at ~4x by design.
homicide_diverse.label_raw: Negligent homicide / homicidio culposo: Art. 60 caps at 1/4 of intentional penalty, ~3-6 years for basic culposo
homicide_diverse.source_citation: Mexico, Codigo Penal Federal Arts. 60+302 (Justia Mexico); culposo term derived via Art. 60 1/4 rule, state codes vary

homicide_diverse.summary: Egypt Penal Code Art. 230 punishes premeditated murder by death (operating alongside qisas, with heirs' pardon able to substitute); a capital construct with mixed Islamic/civil-law character, the top intent tier.
homicide_diverse.label_raw: Premeditated murder (Art. 230): death penalty (alongside qisas; heirs' pardon can substitute)
homicide_diverse.source_citation: Egypt, Penal Code Law No. 58 of 1937 Art. 230 (EIPR, The Death Penalty in Egyptian Law)

homicide_diverse.summary: Egypt Penal Code Art. 234 punishes deliberate killing without premeditation by permanent or temporary hard labour (death if accompanied by another felony); a custodial construct, the middle intent tier.
homicide_diverse.label_raw: Deliberate killing without premeditation (Art. 234): permanent or temporary hard labour; death if with another felony
homicide_diverse.source_citation: Egypt, Penal Code Law No. 58 of 1937 Art. 234 (UNODC SHERLOC)

homicide_diverse.summary: Egypt Penal Code Art. 238 punishes causing death by negligence/recklessness by >=6 months plus a nominal EGP 200 fine (1937 figure, ~cents in 2024 USD and inflation-voided), rising to 5-10 years for aggravators; a custodial construct illustrating that nominal monetary penalties in old codes are not reliable calibration anchors.
homicide_diverse.label_raw: Causing death by negligence/recklessness (Art. 238): >=6 months and/or fine up to EGP 200 base; up to 5 years if under influence; 1-7 years if >=3 victims; 1-10 years if intoxicated with mass casualties
homicide_diverse.source_citation: Egypt, Penal Code Law No. 58 of 1937 Art. 238 (Ahram Online); EGP 200 is the 1937 nominal figure, negligible in 2024 USD

vsl_diverse.summary: Stated-preference (payment-card WTP) value of a statistical life for urban Chinese residents (Shanghai, Nanning, Jiujiang), ~$615,000 in 2016 USD normalized to ~$800,000 (2024 USD); this is ex ante willingness-to-pay for a 5-in-10,000 annual mortality-risk reduction, not ex post compensation.
vsl_diverse.source_citation: Hoffmann, Krupnick & Qin (2017), Journal of Benefit-Cost Analysis, 'Building a Set of Internationally Comparable VSL Studies: Estimates of Chinese Willingness to Pay to Reduce Mortality Risk'. https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-benefit-cost-analysis/article/building-a-set-of-internationally-comparable-value-of-statistical-life-studies-estimates-of-chinese-willingness-to-pay-to-reduce-mortality-risk/F0736C663CC8C30263752C6E7D187526 (2016->2024 CPI x1.30, researcher arithmetic)

vsl_diverse.summary: Contingent-valuation (WTP) value of a statistical life from six representative Chinese cities to reduce air-pollution death risk, CNY 4.76M = ~US$690,000 (2019) normalized to ~$830,000 (2024 USD); WTP construct, not compensation.
vsl_diverse.source_citation: Chinese Journal of Population, Resources and Environment (2023). https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2325426223000530 (USD-conversion-year uncertain; researcher arithmetic)

vsl_diverse.summary: Hedonic-wage (compensating wage differential, revealed-preference) value of a statistical life for blue-collar male manufacturing workers in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, INR 44.69M = ~$0.64M (2018 USD) normalized to ~$0.80M (2024 USD); WTP-type anchor, not compensation.
vsl_diverse.source_citation: 'Value of statistical life in India: A hedonic wage approach' (Madheswaran-style), IDEAS/RePEc working paper. https://ideas.repec.org/p/sch/wpaper/407.html (benefit-transfer cross-checks give wider $0.5-1.6M range; USD-year basis uncertain)

vsl_diverse.summary: No clean single-figure willingness-to-pay VSL was extractable for Brazil; the recent hedonic-wage study (PNS 2019, quantile regression with sample-selection correction) reports a Value of Statistical Injury rather than a headline VSL, so Brazil is flagged as not yet anchorable.
vsl_diverse.label_raw: Brazilian hedonic-wage VSI (PNS 2019) - no headline VSL
vsl_diverse.source_citation: ResearchGate 'Inequality and the Value of a Statistical Life'; Brazilian hedonic-wage paper using PNS 2019. Not yet anchorable - needs direct primary-source fetch before use.

vsl_diverse.summary: Implied 'value of a death averted' (VSL proxy) for South Africa derived from health-spending elasticity on the age-standardised death rate, ZAR 1.89M (2020) ~ US$120,000-130,000 (2024 USD); this is a government revealed/supply-side valuation via budget, not stated willingness-to-pay, making it a methodologically weaker WTP anchor.
vsl_diverse.label_raw: ZAR 1.472M (2015) / ZAR 1.89M (2020) value of a death averted
vsl_diverse.source_citation: Edoka & Stacey (health-spending elasticity), cited in Barr et al., South African Journal of Economic and Management Sciences (2023, alcohol cost-benefit analysis). https://sajems.org/index.php/sajems/article/view/5314/2956 (implied value, ZAR1.89M 2020 at ~16.5/USD then CPI-adjusted)

vsl_diverse.summary: Survey/opinion-poll 'cost of financial compensation for death' for Russia, ~$71,500 (early 2015) normalized to ~$94,000 (2024 USD), with a broader literature range of $40,000-$2,000,000; journalistic secondary source, included only to bracket the low end of the WTP spectrum.
vsl_diverse.label_raw: ~$71,500 (2015) cost of financial compensation for death
vsl_diverse.source_citation: The Bell, 'The value of a Russian life' (journalistic secondary source citing Russian polling). https://en.thebell.io/the-value-of-a-russian-life/ (not peer-reviewed; flag for replacement with academic source)

vsl_diverse.summary: Hedonic-wage value of a statistical life for Thailand (Labour Force Survey + Social Security Office, 2012-2014 averaged), mean $1.21M (2011 USD) normalized to ~$1.7M (2024 USD), with income elasticity 1.488 (income-elastic); revealed-preference WTP anchor.
vsl_diverse.label_raw: Mean VSL $1.21M / median $0.66M (2011 USD), income elasticity 1.488
vsl_diverse.source_citation: Witvorapong & Komonpaisarn (2020), Journal of Consumer Policy. https://ideas.repec.org/a/kap/jcopol/v43y2020i3d10.1007_s10603-019-09431-2.html (2011->2024 CPI x1.41, researcher arithmetic)

vsl_diverse.summary: Updated hedonic log-wage value of a statistical life for Thailand (national labour-force survey + workplace-risk data 2014-2021), US$2,015,694 (2021, PPP-adjusted); PPP basis means it is not directly comparable to the market-exchange-rate figures.
vsl_diverse.source_citation: Journal of Applied Economics and Management Strategy. http://kuojs.lib.ku.ac.th/index.php/jaems/article/view/6254 (PPP-adjusted; stated as 2021 PPP USD)

vsl_diverse.summary: Best hedonic-wage value of a statistical life for Chile (Heckit 2SLS correcting endogeneity/selection; CASEN 2013 + occupational-risk records), US$3.73M (2013 USD) normalized to ~$5.0M (2024 USD), 95% CI US$3.4M-4.0M; revealed-preference WTP anchor and the high end of this sample.
vsl_diverse.source_citation: Mardones & Riquelme (2018), Latin American Research Review. https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/latin-american-research-review/article/estimation-of-the-value-of-statistical-life-in-chile-and-extrapolation-to-other-latin-american-countries/5F9D844230E591849C0AA11BD4527A19 (2013->2024 CPI x1.34, researcher arithmetic)

vsl_diverse.summary: Primary wage-risk (compensating wage differential) value of a statistical life for Mexico City metro workers (~600 workers, perceived and actuarial occupational risk), US$235,000-325,000 (2002 USD) normalized to ~$410,000-565,000 (2024 USD); the genuine primary Mexican WTP/wage-risk anchor (recorded at the ~$490k midpoint).
vsl_diverse.source_citation: Hammitt & Ibarraran (2006), Health Economics. https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/hec.1137 (2002->2024 CPI x1.74, researcher arithmetic; 2024-USD midpoint of $410k-$565k range)

vsl_diverse.summary: Benefit-transfer value of a statistical life for Mexico, US$2.0M base (2021 USD) normalized to ~$2.3M (2024 USD) with a sub-national range of $0.4M (Chiapas) to $3.3M (Mexico City); extrapolated downward from an OECD VSL of $9M with income elasticity 1.0, so it is not an independent primary national estimate.
vsl_diverse.source_citation: Becerra-Perez et al. (2024), Int. J. Environmental Research and Public Health, PMC11032065. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11032065/ (OECD benefit-transfer, income elasticity 1.0; 2021->2024 CPI x1.16, researcher arithmetic)

historical_codes.summary: Hammurabi SS196-197: destroying the eye or breaking the bone of a social equal (awilum) is punished by talio (in-kind retaliation), not cash — a 1.0 in-kind equivalence of the same injury rather than a compensation price.
historical_codes.label_raw: Code of Hammurabi SS196-197 (eye/bone of an awilum: talio)
historical_codes.source_citation: Code of Hammurabi SS196-197; eHammurabi https://ehammurabi.org/law/196 ; Wikipedia 'Code of Hammurabi'

historical_codes.summary: Hammurabi S198: the eye or bone of a commoner (muskenum) is priced at a fixed compensation of 1 mina of silver (60 shekels) — the cash-priced reference rung for this victim class — rather than talio.
historical_codes.label_raw: Code of Hammurabi S198 (muskenum eye/bone = 1 mina = 60 shekels)
historical_codes.source_citation: Code of Hammurabi S198; eHammurabi https://ehammurabi.org/law/198

historical_codes.summary: Hammurabi S199: injuring a slave's eye or bone is compensated at half the slave's market value, paid to the owner — encoding the slave as chattel so the injury value scales with property price, a separate property-based scale rather than a human life-price.
historical_codes.label_raw: Code of Hammurabi S199 (slave eye/bone = 1/2 chattel market value, paid to owner)
historical_codes.source_citation: Code of Hammurabi S199; eHammurabi https://ehammurabi.org/law/199

historical_codes.summary: Hammurabi SS200-201: an equal's knocked-out tooth draws talio while a commoner's tooth is compensated at 1/3 mina (20 shekels) — within-code ratio places the commoner's tooth at ~0.33 of the commoner's eye/bone, the cheapest body part priced.
historical_codes.label_raw: Code of Hammurabi SS200-201 (commoner tooth = 1/3 mina = 20 shekels = 0.33 x eye)
historical_codes.source_citation: Code of Hammurabi SS200-201; eHammurabi assault group https://ehammurabi.org/lch/law-groups/assault

historical_codes.summary: Hammurabi SS209-210: causing a free man's daughter to miscarry by striking her is compensated at 10 shekels of silver; if she herself dies, talio applies to the striker's own daughter (life-for-life), with the same act against lower classes priced far lower.
historical_codes.label_raw: Code of Hammurabi SS209-210 (free man's daughter miscarriage = 10 shekels; her death = talio on striker's daughter)
historical_codes.source_citation: Code of Hammurabi SS209-210; eHammurabi assault group https://ehammurabi.org/lch/law-groups/assault

historical_codes.summary: Roman Twelve Tables VIII.2: a maimed/broken limb (membrum ruptum) is the top injury tier, punished by talio in kind unless the parties agree composition — quasi-irreparable, with no fixed cash ceiling.
historical_codes.label_raw: Twelve Tables VIII.2 (membrum ruptum: talio unless composition)
historical_codes.source_citation: Twelve Tables VIII.2; Perseus Dict. of Greek & Roman Antiquities 'Talio' https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus:text:1999.04.0063:alphabetic+letter%3DT:entry%3Dtalio-cn

historical_codes.summary: Roman Twelve Tables VIII.3: a broken bone (os fractum) of a free man is compensated at 300 asses and of a slave at 150 asses — a clean 2:1 free:slave status ratio within the bone tier.
historical_codes.label_raw: Twelve Tables VIII.3 (os fractum: free man = 300 asses, slave = 150 asses; free:slave = 2:1)
historical_codes.source_citation: Twelve Tables VIII.3; Perseus 'Talio'/'Iniuria' https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus:text:1999.04.0063:entry=injuria-cn ; Loeb The Twelve Tables (1938) https://www.loebclassics.com/view/twelve_tables/1938/pb_LCL329.477.xml

historical_codes.summary: Roman Twelve Tables VIII.4: a minor injury/insult (iniuria) is compensated at 25 asses — within-code, 1/12 of a free man's broken bone (300 asses), the lowest priced rung above the talio/bone tiers.
historical_codes.label_raw: Twelve Tables VIII.4 (iniuria = 25 asses = 1/12 of free man's broken bone)

historical_codes.summary: Law of Aethelberht (Kent): the death of a freeman (ceorl) is compensated by a wergild of 100 shillings, the reference life-price (1.0) against which all Kentish body-part prices are scaled.
historical_codes.label_raw: Law of Aethelberht (Kent): freeman (ceorl) wergild = 100 shillings (life reference = 1.0)
historical_codes.source_citation: Law of Aethelberht (Kent, c.600); Museum Facts 'Anglo-Saxon Wergild' https://museumfacts.co.uk/history-of-personal-injury-law-anglo-saxon-wergild/

historical_codes.summary: Law of Aethelberht (Kent): loss of a foot or an eye is compensated at 50 shillings each — exactly 0.50 of the freeman's wergild, placing major limb/eye loss at half a life.
historical_codes.label_raw: Law of Aethelberht (Kent): foot = 50 sh (0.50), eye = 50 sh (0.50)
historical_codes.source_citation: Law of Aethelberht (Kent); Museum Facts https://museumfacts.co.uk/history-of-personal-injury-law-anglo-saxon-wergild/ ; Medievalists.net https://www.medievalists.net/2018/01/anglo-saxon-punishments-price-pinky/

historical_codes.summary: Law of Aethelberht (Kent): fine-grained body-part gradation — thumb = 20 shillings (0.20), individual fingers 4-11 sh (~0.04-0.11), front tooth = 6 sh (0.06), molar/other tooth = 1 sh (0.01) — with the tooth the cheapest rung at ~0.01 of a life.
historical_codes.label_raw: Law of Aethelberht (Kent): thumb=20sh(0.20), fingers=4-11sh, front tooth=6sh(0.06), molar=1sh(0.01)

historical_codes.summary: Law of Aethelberht (Kent): loss of the generative/reproductive organ ('kindling limb') is compensated at 300 shillings = 3x the full freeman wergild — pricing loss of procreative capacity above a single death, signaling heavy weighting of lineage/reproductive future.
historical_codes.label_raw: Law of Aethelberht (Kent): reproductive organ = 300 sh = 3x wergild (above a life)

historical_codes.summary: Laws of Alfred (Wessex, c.890): independent ~3-centuries-later corroboration in the same tradition — eye = 66 shillings, foot at the knee = 80, great toe = 20, loss of procreative capacity = 80 — notably pricing the genital injury at foot-tier (NOT above a life), showing the 'reproduction > death' weighting was not universal even within one tradition.
historical_codes.label_raw: Laws of Alfred (Wessex): eye=66sh, foot(at knee)=80sh, great toe=20sh, procreative capacity=80sh (foot-tier, not above life)
historical_codes.source_citation: Laws of Alfred (Wessex, c.890); Medievalists.net 'Price of a Pinky' https://www.medievalists.net/2018/01/anglo-saxon-punishments-price-pinky/

historical_codes.summary: Cyfraith Hywel (Wales): the galanas (blood-price for the death) of a free man (bonheddig) is 3,780 pence = 63 cows, the reference life-price (1.0) in the two-layer galanas/sarhaed system where galanas = 3 x sarhaed.
historical_codes.label_raw: Cyfraith Hywel (Wales): free man galanas = 3,780 pence = 63 cows (life reference = 1.0)
historical_codes.source_citation: Cyfraith Hywel / Galanas; Wikipedia 'Galanas' https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galanas ; Wikipedia 'Cyfraith Hywel' https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyfraith_Hywel

historical_codes.summary: Cyfraith Hywel (Wales): the base sarhaed (insult/injury price) = galanas / 3 = 1,260 pence, i.e. 0.33 of a free man's life-price — the structural one-third rule linking the dignity/injury layer to the blood-price layer.
historical_codes.label_raw: Cyfraith Hywel (Wales): base sarhaed = galanas/3 = 1,260 pence (0.33 of life)

historical_codes.summary: Cyfraith Hywel (Wales): the 'nine limbs of equal value' (two hands, two eyes, two feet, two lips/eyelids, nose) are each compensated at 480 pence ~0.127 of a free man's galanas (~1/8 of a life); all nine sum to ~4,320 pence, exceeding one life — a coherent severity ceiling.
historical_codes.label_raw: Cyfraith Hywel (Wales): each of nine equal-value limbs = 480 pence (~0.127 of life); all nine > one life

historical_codes.summary: Cyfraith Hywel (Wales): distinctive status design — the physical-loss component is egalitarian and fixed regardless of rank (a king's eye = a villein's eye = 480 pence), while only the dignity/insult component (sarhaed) scales with rank (queen's/heir's sarhaed = 1/3 of the king's).
historical_codes.label_raw: Cyfraith Hywel (Wales): body-part value flat across rank (king's eye = villein's eye = 480 pence); only sarhaed status-graded
